jelet-2023-q001.conceptSummary: Square the symmetric matrix and read off the off-diagonal entry $\beta$.

steps.title: Multiply
steps.bodyLatex: $A^{2} = \begin{pmatrix} x & y \\ y & x \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} x & y \\ y & x \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} x^{2} + y^{2} & 2xy \\ 2xy & x^{2} + y^{2} \end{pmatrix}$.

steps.title: Match with the given form
steps.bodyLatex: $A^{2}$ has the printed shape $\begin{pmatrix} \alpha & \beta \\ \beta & \alpha \end{pmatrix}$ with $\alpha = x^{2} + y^{2}$ and $\beta = 2xy$.

verification.note: SymPy: A^2 = [[x^2+y^2, 2xy], [2xy, x^2+y^2]]; solve(K xy/2 = 2xy) -> K = 4.

jelet-2023-q002.conceptSummary: $P$ is orthogonal ($P^{T}P = I$), so powers of $Q = PAP^{T}$ telescope: $Q^{n} = PA^{n}P^{T}$.

steps.title: $P$ is orthogonal
steps.bodyLatex: $P$ is the rotation matrix with $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, $\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$: $P^{T}P = \begin{pmatrix} \tfrac{3}{4} + \tfrac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & \tfrac{1}{4} + \tfrac{3}{4} \end{pmatrix} = I$, so $P^{T}P = PP^{T} = I$.

steps.title: Telescope the powers
steps.bodyLatex: $Q^{2} = PAP^{T}\,PAP^{T} = PA(P^{T}P)AP^{T} = PA^{2}P^{T}$, and by induction $Q^{99} = PA^{99}P^{T}$.

steps.title: Sandwich with $P^{T}$ and $P$
steps.bodyLatex: $P^{T}Q^{99}P = (P^{T}P)A^{99}(P^{T}P) = A^{99}$. Options (A), (B) do not involve $A$, and (C) $A \neq A^{99}$ in general (e.g. $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$). Answer: (D).

verification.note: SymPy: P^T P = I; P^T Q^3 P = A^3 for a generic A; exact P^T Q^99 P = A^99 for A = [[1,1],[0,2]], differs from P^99, (P^T)^99, A.

jelet-2023-q003.conceptSummary: Rank $1$ means every row is a multiple of the first (non-zero) row $(-1, 2, 5)$.

steps.title: Compare the first two columns
steps.bodyLatex: Row 2 $= (2, -4, a-4)$: its first two entries are $-2\times(-1, 2)$, so we need $a - 4 = -2\times 5 = -10$, i.e. $a = -6$.

steps.title: Check row 3
steps.bodyLatex: Row 3 $= (1, -2, a+1)$ is $-1\times(-1, 2)$ in the first two entries, so we need $a + 1 = -5$, i.e. $a = -6$ again. Both conditions agree.

steps.title: Verify
steps.bodyLatex: With $a = -6$ the rows are $(-1, 2, 5)$, $(2, -4, -10)$, $(1, -2, -5)$, all multiples of $(-1, 2, 5)$, so the rank is $1$. For $a = -1, -2, 4$ the rank is $2$. Answer: (C).

verification.note: SymPy: rank of the matrix at a = -1, -2, -6, 4 is 2, 2, 1, 2.

jelet-2023-q004.conceptSummary: Logs of GP terms are linear in the term number, so column 1 is a combination of columns 2 and 3.

steps.title: Write the GP terms
steps.bodyLatex: Let the GP have first term $A_{0}$ and ratio $R$. Then $x = A_{0}R^{p-1}$, $y = A_{0}R^{q-1}$, $z = A_{0}R^{r-1}$, so $\log x = (\log A_{0} - \log R) + p\log R$, and similarly for $y$ and $z$.

steps.title: Column operation
steps.bodyLatex: $C_{1} \to C_{1} - (\log R)\,C_{2} - (\log A_{0} - \log R)\,C_{3}$ turns every entry of column 1 into $0$. Hence $|A| = 0$.

steps.title: Judge the options
steps.bodyLatex: $|A| = 0$, so $A$ is singular (A). An orthogonal matrix has $|A| = \pm 1$, so (B) is false. (C) and (D) claim $|A| = r\log y$ or $q\log z$, which are non-zero in general (e.g. $A_{0} = 2$, $R = 3$, $q = 2$, $r = 4$ gives $r\log y = 4\log 6 \neq 0$). Answer: (A).

verification.note: SymPy: det with log x = log A0 + (p-1) log R etc. expands to 0; r log y = 4 log 6 != 0 for a sample GP.

jelet-2023-q005.conceptSummary: Three points are collinear iff the area determinant vanishes.

steps.title: Expand
steps.bodyLatex: Expanding along the new row 3 gives $1\cdot\begin{vmatrix} a_{1} & b_{1} \\ a_{2} & b_{2} \end{vmatrix} = a_{1}b_{2} - a_{2}b_{1}$.

steps.title: Collinearity condition
steps.bodyLatex: Collinear $\iff a_{1}b_{2} - a_{2}b_{1} = 0 \iff a_{1}b_{2} = b_{1}a_{2}$. The other three relations are not multiples of this determinant. Answer: (A).

verification.note: SymPy: determinant = a1 b2 - a2 b1; only option A is proportional to it.

jelet-2023-q006.conceptSummary: Infinitely many solutions need $\det = 0$ AND a consistent system. Here the only singular value $k = -1$ makes the system inconsistent, so no option is correct. WBJEEB withdrew the item.

steps.title: Test $k = -1$
steps.bodyLatex: For $k = -1$ the third equation reads $x + y + z = 4$, while the first says $x + y + z = 1$. The system is inconsistent (rank of the coefficient matrix $2$, rank of the augmented matrix $3$), so it has no solution.

steps.title: Test the options
steps.bodyLatex: For $k = 0, 3, 2, -2$, $\Delta = -1, -4, -3, 1 \neq 0$, so Cramer's rule gives a unique solution. For no real $k$ are there infinitely many solutions.

steps.title: Why the item was withdrawn
steps.bodyLatex: No option (indeed no real $k$) satisfies the stem, so the single-correct question has no valid answer. The WBJEEB final key JEEB/Reg-267/23 marks Q6 W (withdrawn).

steps.title: Marking
steps.bodyLatex: Q6 is a Category-I item marked W (withdrawn). It awards the full $+1$ mark ($+12$ twelfths) to every candidate, whatever they marked.

verification.note: SymPy: det = -(k+1); at k = -1 rank C = 2, rank [C|b] = 3 (inconsistent); det != 0 for every option -> no option correct -> W, +1 mark (+12 twelfths) to all.

jelet-2023-q007.conceptSummary: A product of $\operatorname{cis}$ factors adds the arguments (De Moivre).

steps.title: Add the arguments
steps.bodyLatex: $f_{r}(\alpha) = \operatorname{cis}\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{r^{2}}(1 + 2 + \cdots + r)\right) = \operatorname{cis}\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{r^{2}}\cdot\dfrac{r(r+1)}{2}\right) = \operatorname{cis}\left(\dfrac{\alpha(r+1)}{2r}\right)$. (The last factor $\operatorname{cis}\dfrac{\alpha}{r} = \operatorname{cis}\dfrac{r\alpha}{r^{2}}$ is the $r$-th term.)

verification.note: SymPy: sum_{j=1}^{r} j alpha/r^2 = alpha(r+1)/(2r); limit of exp(i pi (n+1)/(2n)) = I.

steps.title: Note on labelling
steps.bodyLatex: The expression is cyclic. Swapping the labels of $b$ and $c$ (equivalently $\omega \leftrightarrow \omega^{2}$) gives $3\omega$, option (C). The official key takes the conventional labelling above and lists (D). Options (A) and (B) are never attained.

verification.note: SymPy: cubic(y+1) = y^3 + 27; with roots 1-3, 1-3w, 1-3w^2 the sum is 3w^2 (swapped labels give 3w); key D kept.

jelet-2023-q009.conceptSummary: Rotating about $A$ changes the inclination of $AB$ from $45^{\circ}$ to $60^{\circ}$ while keeping $A$ on the line.

steps.title: Inclination of $AB$
steps.bodyLatex: Slope of $AB = \dfrac{1 - 0}{3 - 2} = 1$, so $AB$ makes $45^{\circ}$ with the $x$-axis.

steps.title: Rotate
steps.bodyLatex: An anticlockwise rotation of $15^{\circ}$ gives inclination $60^{\circ}$, slope $\tan 60^{\circ} = \sqrt{3}$. The line still passes through $A(2, 0)$.

verification.note: SymPy: tan(pi/4 + pi/12) = sqrt(3); only option D is proportional to y - sqrt(3)(x - 2).

jelet-2023-q010.conceptSummary: Intersect the line with the parabola and measure the distance between the two points.

steps.title: Endpoints
steps.bodyLatex: $x = \dfrac{9}{2} \Rightarrow y = 6$, and $x = \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow y = -2$. The chord joins $\left(\dfrac{9}{2}, 6\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, -2\right)$.

verification.note: SymPy: intersections (1/2, -2), (9/2, 6); distance 4 sqrt(5).

jelet-2023-q011.conceptSummary: Eliminate $t$ with $\sec^{2}t - \tan^{2}t = 1$ to get a hyperbola centred at $(-1, 2)$.

steps.title: Hyperbola data
steps.bodyLatex: Centre $(-1, 2)$, transverse axis horizontal, $a^{2} = 1$, $b^{2} = 9$, so $c = \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}} = \sqrt{10}$.

steps.title: Foci
steps.bodyLatex: $(-1 \pm \sqrt{10}, 2)$. Option (C) uses $c = \sqrt{8}$ (that would be $\sqrt{b^{2} - a^{2}}$), and (A), (D) shift the centre. Answer: (B).

verification.note: SymPy: (x+1)^2 - (y-2)^2/9 - 1 vanishes on the parametrisation; c = sqrt(10); foci (-1 ± sqrt(10), 2).

jelet-2023-q012.conceptSummary: Expand with the vector triple product: $\vec{p} \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) = \vec{a}(\vec{p}\cdot\vec{b}) - \vec{b}(\vec{p}\cdot\vec{a})$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: It is a scalar multiple of $\vec{a} - \vec{b}$. Answer: (B).

verification.note: SymPy: for three pairs of rational unit vectors (a+b)x(axb) = (1 + a.b)(a - b) and is parallel only to a - b.

jelet-2023-q013.conceptSummary: The tangent direction is $\vec{r}\,'(t)$; normalise it at $t = 2$.

steps.title: Unit tangent
steps.bodyLatex: $\hat{T} = \dfrac{1}{6}(4\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) = \dfrac{1}{3}(2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k})$. Option (A) has the right direction but magnitude $\sqrt{3}$, so it is not a unit vector. Answer: (D).

verification.note: SymPy: sin(pi cos^2 x) - sin(pi sin^2 x) simplifies to 0; limit = pi.

jelet-2023-q015.conceptSummary: For a finite limit at $x = 2$ the numerator must vanish there; then the limit must equal $f(2) = 2$.

steps.title: Numerator at $x = 2$
steps.bodyLatex: $4 - 2(A + 2) + A = -A$. The denominator vanishes at $x = 2$, so a finite limit needs $-A = 0$, i.e. $A = 0$.

steps.title: Continuity
steps.bodyLatex: $\lim_{x\to 2} f(x) = 2 = f(2)$, so $f$ is continuous. For $A = 1, -1, 2$ the numerator is non-zero at $2$ and the limit is infinite. Answer: (A).

verification.note: SymPy: numerator(2) = -A -> A = 0; limit at 2 equals 2 only for A = 0.

jelet-2023-q016.conceptSummary: Differentiate from first principles using the functional equation, then integrate with $f(0) = 0$.

steps.title: Integrate
steps.bodyLatex: $f(x) = 3x + \dfrac{x^{2}}{2} + C$ and $f(0) = 0$ gives $C = 0$. Check: $f(x + y) - f(x) - f(y) = \dfrac{(x+y)^{2} - x^{2} - y^{2}}{2} = xy$. Answer: (B).

verification.note: SymPy: f' = 3 + x, f = 3x + x^2/2; only option B satisfies f(x+y) = f(x)+f(y)+xy, f(0)=0, lim f(h)/h = 3.

jelet-2023-q017.conceptSummary: A $0/0$ form: apply L'Hospital's rule with the chain rule for the square roots.

steps.title: Check the form
steps.bodyLatex: $\sqrt{f(a)} - a = \sqrt{a^{2}} - a = 0$ and $\sqrt{\phi(a)} - b = 0$ (with $a, b > 0$), so the limit is $0/0$.

verification.note: SymPy: concrete f, phi with f(a)=a^2, phi(a)=b^2, f'(a)=3phi'(a) for (a,b) = (2,5), (3,1/2), (7,4) give limits 3b/a.

jelet-2023-q018.conceptSummary: Rolle's hypotheses hold ($f(-3) = f(0) = 0$); solve $f'(c) = 0$ inside $(-3, 0)$.

steps.title: Pick the root in $(-3, 0)$
steps.bodyLatex: $f'(c) = 0 \Rightarrow c = 3$ or $c = -2$. Only $c = -2$ lies in $(-3, 0)$. The endpoints $-3$ and $0$ are not admissible. Answer: (C).

jelet-2023-q019.conceptSummary: Find the parameter of $M$ from both coordinate equations, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}$.

verification.note: SymPy: common t = 2; slope (4t-2)/(2t+3) = 6/7.

jelet-2023-q020.conceptSummary: Differentiate both coordinates with respect to $\theta$; a zero $dy/d\theta$ with non-zero $dx/d\theta$ means a horizontal tangent.

steps.title: At $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$
steps.bodyLatex: $\cos 3\theta = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{2} = 0$ while $\dfrac{dx}{d\theta} = -\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{1/2}} = -\sqrt{2}\,a \neq 0$. So $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$ and the tangent is parallel to the $x$ axis. Answer: (A).

verification.note: SymPy: at theta = pi/6, dx/dtheta = -sqrt(2) a, dy/dtheta = 0 -> slope 0.

jelet-2023-q021.conceptSummary: Complete the squares to get $\min f$ and $\max g$, then compare.

verification.note: SymPy: min f = 2c^2 - b^2, max g = b^2 + c^2; c^2 > 2b^2 matches only option B on a 13x13 grid of (b, c).

jelet-2023-q022.conceptSummary: $u = \log F$ with $F$ homogeneous of degree $2$; Euler's theorem gives $xu_{x} + yu_{y} = \dfrac{xF_{x} + yF_{y}}{F} = 2$.

steps.title: Degree of homogeneity
steps.bodyLatex: The numerator $x^{3} + x^{2}y - y^{3}$ has degree $3$ and the denominator $x - y$ degree $1$, so $F = \dfrac{x^{3} + x^{2}y - y^{3}}{x - y}$ is homogeneous of degree $2$: $F(sx, sy) = s^{2}F(x, y)$.

steps.title: Apply to $u = \log F$
steps.bodyLatex: $x\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x} + y\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y} = \dfrac{xF_{x} + yF_{y}}{F} = \dfrac{2F}{F} = 2$. Answer: (C).

verification.note: SymPy: F(sx, sy)/F(x, y) = s^2; x u_x + y u_y simplifies to 2.

jelet-2023-q024.conceptSummary: Substitute $u = \log x$: the integral becomes $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{2007}\pi\cos(\pi u)\,du$.

steps.title: Substitution
steps.bodyLatex: $u = \log x$, $du = \dfrac{dx}{x}$. The limits $x = 1 \to u = 0$ and $x = e^{2007} \to u = 2007$.

verification.note: SymPy: substitution x = e^u maps the integrand to pi cos(pi u); integral 0..2007 = 0.

jelet-2023-q025.conceptSummary: The relation forces $h$ to be the constant $-5$; then $fg$ is anti-symmetric about $x = a/2$ and integrates to $0$.

steps.title: Solve for $h$
steps.bodyLatex: Replace $x$ by $a - x$: $3h(a - x) - 4h(x) = 5$. Together with $3h(x) - 4h(a - x) = 5$, subtracting gives $7h(x) = 7h(a - x)$, so $h(x) = h(a - x)$ and then $-h(x) = 5$, i.e. $h \equiv -5$.

steps.title: Use $x \to a - x$
steps.bodyLatex: $J = \displaystyle\int_{0}^{a} f(x)g(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{a} f(a - x)g(a - x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{a} f(x)\,(-g(x))\,dx = -J$, so $J = 0$ and $I = 0$. Answer: (D).

verification.note: SymPy: the 2x2 linear system gives h(x) = h(a-x) = -5; integral of f g h over six sample (f, g, a) triples is 0.

jelet-2023-q026.conceptSummary: The parabolas $y = x^{2}$ and $y = \sqrt{x}$ meet at $x = 0$ and $x = 1$; integrate the gap.

steps.title: Intersection
steps.bodyLatex: $x = y^{2}$ is $y = \sqrt{x}$ in the first quadrant. $x^{2} = \sqrt{x} \Rightarrow x^{4} = x \Rightarrow x = 0, 1$.

steps.title: Set up
steps.bodyLatex: On $[0, 1]$, $\sqrt{x} \geq x^{2}$, so the area is $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}(\sqrt{x} - x^{2})\,dx$.

verification.note: SymPy: integrate(sqrt(x) - x^2, (x, 0, 1)) = 1/3.

jelet-2023-q027.conceptSummary: Homogeneous equation: put $y = vx$, then separate the variables.

steps.title: Substitute $y = vx$
steps.bodyLatex: $y' = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$, so $v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = v + \dfrac{\phi(v)}{\phi'(v)}$, i.e. $x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{\phi(v)}{\phi'(v)}$.

steps.title: Solution
steps.bodyLatex: $\phi(y/x) = cx$. Check with $\phi(s) = s$: $y = cx^{2}$ satisfies $y' = 2y/x$, while (A)/(B) give $y = cx$ and (C) gives $y^{2} = cx$, which fail. Answer: (D).

verification.note: SymPy: each option family substituted into the ODE for phi(s) = s, e^s, s^2; only D satisfies it.

steps.title: Initial condition
steps.bodyLatex: $y(0) = 0$: $4 + 3 = K = 7$, so $4e^{3x} + 3e^{-4y} = 7$. (B) has the wrong sign in $e^{4y}$, (C) fails at the origin ($2 \neq 1$), and (D) has an impossible negative right side. Answer: (A).

verification.note: SymPy: for each option, implicit y' = -F_x/F_y compared with e^{3x+4y} and F(0,0) = 0; only A passes.

jelet-2023-q029.conceptSummary: Use the complement: the minimum is at least $5$ iff both numbers come from $\{5, \ldots, 10\}$.

verification.note: SymPy/enumeration: 30 of 45 pairs have min < 5 -> 2/3.

jelet-2023-q030.conceptSummary: From $P(A/B) = P(A)$, the events are independent; compute $P(B)$ and test each option.

steps.title: Independence
steps.bodyLatex: $P(A)P(B) = \dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{8} = P(A\cap B)$, so $A$ and $B$ are independent (A). $P(A\cap B) \neq 0$, so they are not mutually exclusive (B false).

jelet-2023-q031.conceptSummary: Use $(MN)^{T} = N^{T}M^{T}$, $X^{T} = X$, $Z^{T} = -Z$; even powers of $Z$ are symmetric, odd powers skew. All four options are judged.

steps.title: Powers of $Z$
steps.bodyLatex: $(Z^{k})^{T} = (Z^{T})^{k} = (-1)^{k}Z^{k}$: $Z^{4}$ is symmetric, while $Z^{5}$ and $Z^{99}$ are skew symmetric. Powers of $X$ and $Y$ stay symmetric.

steps.title: (A) and (B)
steps.bodyLatex: (A) $M = X^{3}Z^{4} - Z^{4}X^{3}$: $M^{T} = Z^{4}X^{3} - X^{3}Z^{4} = -M$, so it is skew symmetric. (B) $M = X^{5}Z^{5} - Z^{5}X^{5}$: $M^{T} = (-Z^{5})X^{5} - X^{5}(-Z^{5}) = M$, so it is symmetric (not skew in general).

verification.note: SymPy: random integer symmetric X, Y and skew Z (2 draws): A, C satisfy M^T = -M (non-zero); B, D are symmetric non-zero.

jelet-2023-q032.conceptSummary: Factor the determinant: $\Delta = (b^{2} - ac)(a\alpha^{2} + 2b\alpha + c)$. All four options are judged.

steps.title: Column operation
steps.bodyLatex: $C_{3} \to C_{3} - \alpha C_{1} - C_{2}$: rows 1 and 2 of $C_{3}$ become $0$, and row 3 becomes $0 - \alpha(a\alpha + b) - (b\alpha + c) = -(a\alpha^{2} + 2b\alpha + c)$.

steps.title: Expand
steps.bodyLatex: $\Delta = -(a\alpha^{2} + 2b\alpha + c)\begin{vmatrix} a & b \\ b & c \end{vmatrix} = -(a\alpha^{2} + 2b\alpha + c)(ac - b^{2}) = (b^{2} - ac)(a\alpha^{2} + 2b\alpha + c)$.

steps.title: Judge the options
steps.bodyLatex: (B) G.P.: $b^{2} = ac \Rightarrow \Delta = 0$. (D) $a\alpha^{2} + 2b\alpha + c = 0 \Rightarrow \Delta = 0$. (A) A.P. ($2b = a + c$) and (C) H.P. ($b = \frac{2ac}{a+c}$) do not make either factor vanish in general (A.P. $a = 1$, $b = 2$, $c = 3$, $\alpha = 1$ gives $\Delta = 1\cdot 8 = 8 \neq 0$; H.P. $a = 1$, $b = \tfrac{4}{3}$, $c = 2$, $\alpha = 1$ gives $\Delta = -\tfrac{2}{9}\cdot\tfrac{17}{3} \neq 0$).

verification.note: SymPy: factor(det) = -(ac - b^2)(a alpha^2 + 2b alpha + c); vanishes identically under the G.P. and root conditions only.

jelet-2023-q033.conceptSummary: $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \pm \dfrac{i}{2} = e^{\pm i\pi/6}$, so $z = 2\cos\dfrac{2007\pi}{6}$ by De Moivre. All four options are judged.

steps.title: Polar form
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \dfrac{i}{2} = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{6} + i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, and the second number is its conjugate.

steps.title: Judge the options
steps.bodyLatex: (A) $z = 0$ is true. (B) $z = i$ is false. (C) $\operatorname{Re}(z) = 0$, not $> 0$, so false. (D) $\operatorname{Im}(z) = 0$, so false. Answer: (A).

verification.note: SymPy: 2cos(2007 pi/6) = 0; 60-digit mpmath evaluation of the two powers sums to |z| < 1e-40.

jelet-2023-q034.conceptSummary: Put the third vertex at $(t, t + 3)$ and solve $\tfrac{1}{2}|\text{cross product}| = 5$. Two vertices qualify; the official key lists only one.

steps.title: Solve
steps.bodyLatex: $|4t - 4| = 10 \Rightarrow t - 1 = \pm\dfrac{5}{2} \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{7}{2}$ or $t = -\dfrac{3}{2}$. The vertices are $\left(\dfrac{7}{2}, \dfrac{13}{2}\right)$ and $\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{3}{2}\right)$.

steps.title: Judge the options
steps.bodyLatex: (D) $\left(\dfrac{7}{2}, \dfrac{13}{2}\right)$ is on $y = x + 3$ with area $5$, so true. (A) $\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{3}{2}\right)$ is on $y = x + 3$ with area $\tfrac{1}{2}|-6 - 4| = 5$, so also true. (B) $\left(\dfrac{3}{2}, -\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$ is not on the line (area $2$). (C) $\left(\dfrac{7}{2}, \dfrac{14}{3}\right)$ is not on the line.

steps.title: Official key and dispute
steps.bodyLatex: The mathematics gives (A), (D). The official key JEEB/Reg-267/23 lists only (D), and that key is used for scoring here. Under the Category-II rule, marking (D) alone scores the full $2$ marks, while marking (A) as well counts as a wrong option and scores $0$. This is recorded as a key dispute.

verification.note: SymPy: |4t - 4| = 10 -> t = 7/2, -3/2; areas of A..D = 5, 2, 49/12, 5 with A, D on the line. Key dispute: official key D kept; A also correct.

steps.title: Maximise
steps.bodyLatex: By Cauchy–Schwarz, $\vec{U}\cdot(\vec{V}\times\vec{W}) \leq \sqrt{59}$, with equality for $\vec{U} = \dfrac{3\hat{i} - 7\hat{j} - \hat{k}}{\sqrt{59}}$. The maximum is $\sqrt{59}$. Answer: (B).

verification.note: SymPy: V x W = (3, -7, -1), |V x W| = sqrt(59), attained by the unit vector along V x W.

jelet-2023-q036.conceptSummary: $x^{2n} \to \infty$, $1$ or $0$ according as $|x| > 1$, $|x| = 1$ or $|x| < 1$. All four options are judged.

steps.title: $|x| > 1$
steps.bodyLatex: Divide by $x^{2n}$: $\dfrac{1 - x^{-2n}}{1 + x^{-2n}} \to 1$. So (A) is true.

steps.title: (D)
steps.bodyLatex: $f$ is defined for every real $x$ (values $1$, $0$, $-1$), so (D) is false. Answer: (A), (C).

verification.note: SymPy: limits at x = 2, -3, 3/2 give 1; at ±1 give 0; at 1/2, 0, -2/3 give -1.

jelet-2023-q037.conceptSummary: On $xy = 2$ the tangent slope $-2/x^{2}$ is always negative, so every normal has positive slope $x^{2}/2$. All four options are judged.

steps.title: Tangent slope
steps.bodyLatex: $y = \dfrac{2}{x} \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{2}{x^{2}} < 0$ for all $x \neq 0$. The tangent is never horizontal or vertical.

steps.title: Normal slope
steps.bodyLatex: Normal slope $= \dfrac{x^{2}}{2} > 0$. The line $ax + by + c = 0$ has slope $-\dfrac{a}{b}$ ($b \neq 0$), so $-\dfrac{a}{b} > 0$, i.e. $a$ and $b$ have opposite signs.

steps.title: Witnesses
steps.bodyLatex: The normal at $(2, 1)$ is $y - 1 = 2(x - 2)$, i.e. $2x - y - 3 = 0$ ($a > 0$, $b < 0$). Multiplying by $-1$ gives $-2x + y + 3 = 0$ ($a < 0$, $b > 0$). Same-sign pairs (A), (D) would need a negative normal slope, which is impossible.

verification.note: SymPy: tangent slope -2/x0^2, normal slope x0^2/2 > 0; Eq(x0^2/2, -a/b) solvable only when a, b have opposite signs.

jelet-2023-q038.conceptSummary: $z = \tfrac{1}{2}\log(x^{2} + y^{2})$, so $z_{x} = \dfrac{x}{x^{2} + y^{2}}$ and $z_{y} = \dfrac{y}{x^{2} + y^{2}}$. All four options are judged.

steps.title: Partial derivatives
steps.bodyLatex: $z = \dfrac{1}{2}\log(x^{2} + y^{2}) \Rightarrow \dfrac{\partial z}{\partial x} = \dfrac{x}{x^{2} + y^{2}}$ and $\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial y} = \dfrac{y}{x^{2} + y^{2}}$.

steps.title: (B) and (C)
steps.bodyLatex: $xz_{x} + yz_{y} = \dfrac{x^{2} + y^{2}}{x^{2} + y^{2}} = 1$, so (B) is true and (C) is false ($1 \neq \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}$ in general). This is Euler's theorem for a log of a degree-1 homogeneous function.

steps.title: (A) and (D)
steps.bodyLatex: $yz_{x} + xz_{y} = \dfrac{2xy}{x^{2} + y^{2}}$, which is not identically $1$, so (A) is false. $yz_{x} = \dfrac{xy}{x^{2} + y^{2}} = xz_{y}$, so (D) is true.

verification.note: SymPy: z_x = x/(x^2+y^2), z_y = y/(x^2+y^2); x z_x + y z_y = 1, y z_x - x z_y = 0; A and C not identities.

jelet-2023-q039.conceptSummary: $\displaystyle\int_{\pi/2}^{\alpha}\sin x\,dx = -\cos\alpha$, so solve $-\cos\alpha = 2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha$ on $[\pi, 2\pi]$. All four options are judged.

steps.title: Judge the options
steps.bodyLatex: (B) $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$ and (C) $\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$ are solutions. (A) $\dfrac{7\pi}{4}$: $-\cos\alpha = -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ but $\sin 2\alpha = -1$. (D) $\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$: $-\cos\alpha = -\dfrac{1}{2}$ but $\sin 2\alpha = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. Answer: (B), (C).

verification.note: SymPy: -cos(a) - sin(2a) = -(2 sin a + 1) cos a; roots in [pi, 2pi] = 7pi/6, 3pi/2, 11pi/6.

jelet-2023-q040.conceptSummary: With $p = \dfrac{dv}{du}$ the equation $v = up + p^{2}$ is Clairaut's: general solution $v = cu + c^{2}$, singular solution from the $c$-discriminant. All four options are judged.

steps.title: General solution
steps.bodyLatex: Differentiate $v = up + p^{2}$ with respect to $u$: $p = p + (u + 2p)\dfrac{dp}{du}$, so $(u + 2p)\dfrac{dp}{du} = 0$. Taking $\dfrac{dp}{du} = 0$ gives $p = c$ and $v = cu + c^{2}$, i.e. $xy = cy + c^{2}$. This is option (D) with $c_{1} = c^{2}$.

steps.title: Singular solution
steps.bodyLatex: Taking $u + 2p = 0$ gives $p = -\dfrac{u}{2}$, so $v = -\dfrac{u^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{u^{2}}{4} = -\dfrac{u^{2}}{4}$. Back in $x, y$: $xy = -\dfrac{y^{2}}{4} \iff y(y + 4x) = 0$, i.e. $y = 0$ or $y = -4x$. These are options (A) and (C).

steps.title: Reject (B)
steps.bodyLatex: $y = 4x$ gives $v = xy = \dfrac{u^{2}}{4}$, so $p = \dfrac{u}{2}$ and $up + p^{2} = \dfrac{u^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{u^{2}}{4} = \dfrac{3u^{2}}{4} \neq \dfrac{u^{2}}{4}$. It is not a solution.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A), (C), (D). Reading note: (D) $xy = cy + c_{1}$ is the printed form of the general solution and satisfies the equation exactly when $c_{1} = c^{2}$.

verification.note: SymPy: v = cu + c^2 satisfies Clairaut identically; c-discriminant gives v = -u^2/4 <=> y(4x + y) = 0; y = 4x fails (3u^2/4 != u^2/4).
